data.name: Hamd
data.gender_notes: Hamd is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Hamd is derived from the Arabic root 'h-m-d' meaning to praise, give thanks, or express gratitude. In Islamic tradition, Hamd is a common name for boys and is also used as an expression of praise and thanks to Allah. The name Hamd carries the meaning “Praise, Gratitude” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hamd usually hope their child will grow to embody praise, gratitude and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Expressing gratitude and praise to Allah, seeking His blessings
data.etymology: Hamd belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Praise, Gratitude.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hamd total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah The name Hamd carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Hamd (praise) is mentioned in the Quran as a name of Allah and also as a word for praise and thanks. It is said that the Prophet Muhammad (p.b.u.h.) himself used to call Allah by the name Hamd. Ibn Abbas (r.a.) reported that the Prophet (p.b.u.h.) said, 'Allah is Hamd (praise), and Hamd is Allah.'

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Al-Qayyim's I'lam Al-Mu'minin The name Hamd carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Al-Qayyim wrote in his book 'I'lam Al-Mu'minin' that the origin of the name Hamd is from the Arabic word 'Hamdah' which means 'to praise' or 'to extol'. The Prophet Muhammad (p.b.u.h.) used to call Allah by this name and teach his companions to do the same. It is also mentioned in the Quran that Allah is the One who is praised and glorified (Al-Muddaththir:12).
